name: Jane Street
desc: Proprietary trading firm providing liquidity in ETFs, equities, bonds, options, commodities and currencies worldwide.
capacity_detail: Net trading revenue USD 39.6bn in 2025 (Reuters via MarketScreener)
markets: Liquidity provider across ETFs, equities, bonds, options, commodities and currencies; 3,500 employees; has taken no outside capital.
rationale: Record profits and fierce competition for quant talent; F1's engineering and data culture suits graduate recruitment branding.

name: Hudson River Trading
desc: Quantitative trading firm running algorithmic market-making and proprietary trading strategies across global financial markets.
capacity_detail: Trading revenue about USD 12.3bn in 2025 (Reuters sources via MarketScreener)
markets: Algorithmic trading across global markets; record USD 11.4bn trading revenue in Q2 2026 per Hedgeweek.
rationale: Data-driven, engineering-heavy firm competing with Jane Street and Citadel for talent; F1 technology partnership fits recruitment branding.

name: Citadel Securities
desc: Market-making firm providing liquidity in equities, options and other securities to retail brokers and institutions.
capacity_detail: Trading revenue about USD 12.2bn in 2025, up 25% (Reuters sources via MarketScreener)
markets: Market making in equities, options and fixed income for retail brokers and institutions; headquartered in Miami.
rationale: Miami-based market maker with high-speed technology story; Miami Grand Prix and F1's US growth give a home-market platform.

name: IMC Trading
desc: Amsterdam-rooted proprietary trading firm making markets electronically, with large operations in Chicago and other hubs.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 3.12bn and net income USD 968m in 2025
markets: Electronic market making with roots in Amsterdam and large Chicago operations, trading across global exchanges.
rationale: Technology-driven trading house where speed and precision mirror F1; partnership could support global graduate hiring.

name: Optiver
desc: Market-making firm founded in Amsterdam that trades listed derivatives and securities on exchanges across the world.
capacity_detail: Net trading income EUR 4.556bn in 2025; net profit EUR 1.769bn
markets: Offices in Amsterdam, London, Chicago, Austin, New York, Sydney, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Singapore, Taipei and Mumbai.
rationale: Global market maker with over 2,000 staff across three continents; F1's tech audience suits employer branding in key hubs.

name: XTX Markets
desc: Algorithmic trading firm making markets in currencies, equities, fixed income and commodities across 35 countries.
capacity_detail: Combined net revenue GBP 3.93bn across three UK operating entities in 2025
markets: Trades about USD 250bn daily across 35 countries in FX, equities, fixed income and commodities; building Finnish data centre.
rationale: Founder-controlled, highly profitable data and AI-led trader; F1's engineering image suits its technology and recruitment positioning.

name: Saxo Bank
desc: Danish online investment bank offering trading and investing platforms to retail clients and partner institutions.
ownership: private: Bank J. Safra Sarasin (privately owned J. Safra Group)
capacity_detail: Total income EUR 664m in 2025; 1.52m clients; client assets EUR 133bn
markets: More than 1.7m clients and 400 partners; centres in London, Singapore, Amsterdam, Zurich, Dubai and Tokyo.
rationale: New Safra ownership and new CEO may refresh brand; F1 reaches the affluent international investors Saxo targets.

name: Trade Republic
desc: Berlin-based app for retail investors to trade stocks and ETFs and hold savings at low cost.
capacity_detail: Valued at EUR 12.5bn in a EUR 1.2bn secondary share sale, December 2025
markets: German stock-trading app serving retail investors in Europe, profitable for three years per reports of the 2025 sale.
rationale: Decacorn racing to win Europe's retail investors; F1's young European fan base matches its target customer.

name: Scalable Capital
desc: Digital investment platform offering European retail investors trading in ETFs, stocks, funds, bonds and crypto.
capacity_detail: Raised EUR 155m in June 2025, led by Sofina and Noteus; over EUR 470m (USD 535m) raised in total
markets: Retail investors in Europe, focus on Germany; ETFs, stocks, funds, bonds, crypto, derivatives, ELTIFs and securities-backed loans.
rationale: Competing with Trade Republic for European savers; F1 would give pan-European brand reach beyond its German base.

name: Zerodha
desc: Bootstrapped Indian discount stockbroker offering online equity and derivatives trading to millions of retail investors.
capacity_detail: Revenue from operations INR 8,847 crore in FY2025 (year to March 2025); net profit INR 4,237 crore
markets: Indian retail stock and derivatives traders; 7.26m active users and 15.8% market share on NSE.
rationale: Cash-rich market leader in India where F1 interest is growing; limited overseas business makes fit uncertain.

name: Trading 212
desc: Commission-free investing and trading app for retail customers, licensed in the UK, EU and Australia.
capacity_detail: Group revenue GBP 345.8m in 2025 (filed accounts); pre-tax profit GBP 127.7m
markets: Licensed subsidiaries in the UK, Cyprus, Bulgaria, Germany, Australia and Ireland; UK generates about 80% of revenue.
rationale: Spent GBP 88m on marketing in 2025 and growing fast in Europe and Australia, where rivals use F1.

name: Acorns
desc: Consumer app that invests customers' spare change and savings automatically into diversified investment portfolios.
capacity_detail: USD 300m Series F led by TPG at USD 1.9bn valuation (Mar 2022), after USD 105m Series E (2019)
markets: Consumer savings and micro-investing app based in Irvine; source page does not detail its markets.
rationale: US consumer finance brand aimed at young savers; F1's growing US audience overlaps, but no global footprint.

name: FTMO
desc: Czech proprietary-trading firm selling trader evaluations and funded accounts, and owner of broker OANDA.
capacity_detail: Parent OHM consolidated revenue CZK 8.9bn (about USD 427m) in 2025
markets: Prop-trading customers worldwide; UK largest market, United States second via OANDA's licensed US business.

signals.regions: Completed OANDA acquisition, adding licensed US broker (Dec 2025; https://www.financemagnates.com/forex/ftmo-paid-422-million-for-oanda/)

rationale: Fast-growing prop firm that bought OANDA; F1 could unify the brands for traders in the UK and US.

name: ACCM
desc: CFD broker focused on emerging markets, licensed in Australia and South Africa with offshore entities.
capacity_detail: Multi-year Official Partner of the Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP team, announced Feb 2026
sponsorships: Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP (2026, multi-year); ZXMOTO Supersport team (through 2028)
markets: Emerging-market traders, mainly Vietnam and Thailand by web traffic; licences in Australia, South Africa, Seychelles and Vanuatu.
rationale: Already buys MotoGP to reach Southeast Asian traders; F1 is the next step up, as rival brokers show.

name: FPG (Fortune Prime Global)
desc: Online CFD and forex broker holding an Australian ASIC licence and operating in over 30 countries.
capacity_detail: Premium Partner and Official Online Trading Partner of AC Milan, announced Aug 2026
markets: Operates in more than 30 countries; ASIC licence via acquired GMT Markets and Vanuatu authorisation.
rationale: Just entered top-tier sport with AC Milan; F1 offers the global reach brokers like Vantage and AvaTrade already use.

name: Hantec Markets
desc: Multi-regulated online trading broker backed by Hantec Group, also running prop-trading brand Hantec Trader.
capacity_detail: Multi-year UFC sponsorship across APAC events and broadcasts, announced Feb 2026
sponsorships: UFC APAC (2026, multi-year); Atletico de Madrid LatAm online trading partner (2025, multi-year); Fortaleza EC (2025)
markets: CFD and prop-trading clients across Asia-Pacific and Latin America, plus B2B2C partners worldwide.
rationale: Building sports portfolio across UFC and La Liga in APAC and LatAm; F1 races in both regions.

name: EC Markets
desc: London-headquartered forex and CFD broker offering currencies, metals, energies, indices, crypto and stocks.
capacity_detail: Official Global Partner of Liverpool FC under multi-year deal signed Jul 2025
markets: Regulated by FCA, ASIC, FMA, FSCA, UAE CMA, Mauritius FSC and Seychelles FSA; clients worldwide.
rationale: Liverpool deal shows appetite for premium global sport; F1 reaches the same international trader audience.

name: INFINOX
industry: online broker and institutional liquidity provider
desc: Online trading broker founded in 2009, with institutional arm IXO Prime serving hedge funds and prop firms.
capacity_detail: Official Global Partner of Tottenham Hotspur, multi-year deal announced Feb 2026
sponsorships: Tottenham Hotspur (2026, multi-year); Porsche Cup Brazil (2025); polo
markets: Retail and institutional clients; Tottenham activation aimed at Europe, Asia, Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Motor-racing sponsor already (Porsche Cup Brazil); F1 would scale that to a global audience.

name: EBC Financial Group
desc: London-originated forex and CFD broker regulated by the FCA, ASIC and Cayman Islands Monetary Authority.
capacity_detail: FC Barcelona Official Partner in Foreign Exchange for 3.5 years from April 2024
sponsorships: FC Barcelona (2024-2027, APAC, LatAm, Middle East, Africa)
markets: Offices in London, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Sydney, Singapore, Cayman Islands, Bangkok and Limassol.
rationale: Barcelona deal targets APAC, LatAm and Middle East; F1 races in all these regions.

name: HFM
desc: Multi-asset online broker, formerly HotForex, offering forex and CFD trading to retail clients.
capacity_detail: Official Global Partner of Arsenal FC, multi-year deal reported Mar 2026
markets: Retail forex and CFD traders internationally; Arsenal deal covers digital channels and Emirates Stadium matchday branding.
rationale: Finance Magnates notes rivals turning to F1 as HFM signs Arsenal; F1 is the natural next tier.

name: WeTrade
desc: Cyprus-based CFD broker founded in 2015, offering forex, indices and metals trading.
capacity_detail: Multi-year international marketing partnership with NBA's Houston Rockets, Jun 2026
markets: CySEC licence plus permits in Saint Vincent, Australia, Malaysia and Seychelles; not available to US residents.
rationale: Buying NBA and PSG for global visibility; F1 adds Asia and Middle East reach.

name: TMGM
desc: Sydney-based multi-asset broker providing CFD trading in forex, indices, equities and commodities.
capacity_detail: Multiyear partnership with NBA's Brooklyn Nets, signage at all home games from 2025-26
markets: Clients in over 150 countries; Vanuatu-regulated entity among multiple jurisdictions.
rationale: Broker rivals Pepperstone and IC Markets are in F1; TMGM already spends on NBA and Premier League sponsorships.

name: IQ Option
desc: Online trading platform offering CFDs, with group entity Quadcode Markets licensed in Bahamas, Australia and Cyprus.
capacity_detail: Official Racing Partner of United Autosports in FIA WEC, Asian and European Le Mans and 2026 Le Mans
sponsorships: United Autosports, FIA WEC and Le Mans (from Nov 2025)
markets: Retail CFD traders; group licences in the Bahamas, Australia and Cyprus, European presence.
rationale: Already in endurance racing with a McLaren-linked team; F1 is the obvious step up.

name: Moneta Markets
desc: Online forex and CFD broker launched in 2020, separated from Vantage Group in 2022.
capacity_detail: Official regional partner of Atletico de Madrid for APAC, announced Jul 2025
markets: Retail traders in Asia-Pacific and elsewhere; licences in several jurisdictions including Australia and Seychelles.
rationale: Former sister brand Vantage sponsors Ferrari; Moneta could follow to build APAC brand.

name: Trade Nation
desc: FCA-authorised CFD and spread-betting broker with registrations outside the UK and an EU base in Lisbon.
capacity_detail: Sleeve sponsor of Aston Villa, multi-year deal from Jun 2023, still in place Jul 2026
sponsorships: Aston Villa sleeve (2023-); Hampshire Cricket; Southern Vipers
markets: UK retail traders plus registrations outside the UK; EU base in Lisbon; bought FXCM's UK client book.
rationale: Proven Premier League sleeve buyer; F1 would extend brand reach to its growing EU and international customer base.

name: Axi
desc: Online forex and CFD broker with licences in the UK, Dubai, Cyprus and Mauritius.
capacity_detail: Partner of Manchester City and Man City Women; Official LATAM Online Trading Partner of Girona FC (Jan 2026)
sponsorships: Manchester City; Girona FC; Esporte Clube Bahia; DP World Tour (2026); John Stones ambassador
markets: Licences in the UK, Dubai, Cyprus and Mauritius; office in Bangalore; football ties in Europe and Latin America.
rationale: Big sports spender across football and golf whose broker rivals Pepperstone and IC Markets already sponsor F1 teams.

name: Ultima Markets
desc: Online forex and CFD broker that recently gained a UK licence from the FCA.
capacity_detail: Official Regional Partner of Inter Milan in Asia, multi-year deal Aug 2025
markets: Retail traders in Asia, targeting Inter's 295m Asian fans; new UK licence.
rationale: Asia-focused broker using Serie A; F1's Asian races and broker rivals make it a logical upgrade.
